seo.metaDescription: Semax peptide for laboratory research: MEHFPGP sequence, molecular identity, BDNF and neurobiological research, Semax vs Selank and COA checks. RUO only.

blurb: Semax is a synthetic heptapeptide, Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro, related to the ACTH(4-7) sequence and studied in neurotrophin and neurobiological research. Veracue offers it for Research Use Only. This page covers its identity, the published evidence, how it differs from Selank, and how to read a certificate of analysis.

aeo.question: What is Semax?
aeo.answer: Semax is a synthetic heptapeptide with the sequence Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro (MEHFPGP). It joins the ACTH(4-7) fragment to a Pro-Gly-Pro tail and is described in the literature as an analogue related to ACTH(4-10). Published research has examined it mainly in neurotrophin, gene-expression and cerebral-ischemia models, largely in rodents and cell systems. Veracue Semax is offered for Research Use Only and is not intended for human or veterinary use.

sections.heading: Why Researchers Study Semax
body: Semax draws research interest for two connected reasons. It has a short, defined sequence, and published work has linked it to neurotrophin signaling and to injury-model readouts. Those are areas where labs want a well-documented reference peptide.

Most of that work comes from rodents and cell systems, and much of it comes from a small number of Russian research groups. Historical clinical papers exist too, but they sit in a separate evidence tier. The questions below take the topics researchers raise most often, one at a time.

sections.heading: Storage and Documentation
body: Follow the storage conditions provided on the applicable product documentation and vial label. Do not infer product-specific storage conditions from general peptide-handling practices.

Where analytical documentation is available, researchers should review the lot-specific HPLC and mass-spectrometry results rather than assuming a sitewide testing specification. A search for "Semax 10mg" reflects a product-size query. The actual amount supplied should be confirmed from the current product listing rather than inferred from search terminology.
Questions about lot documentation can be sent through Contact Us.

problemSolution.problem: How do I confirm that the material I am researching is actually Semax?
problemSolution.solution: Start with the molecule. Semax is Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro (MEHFPGP), formula C37H51N9O10S, with an average molecular weight near 813.93 g/mol. PubChem lists it as CID 9811102, and FDA's review lists CAS 80714-61-0 and UNII I5FAL2585H for the free peptide. However, public databases hold more than one record, including records for salt forms, so match the exact name and formula rather than the name alone.
problemSolution.explanation: Those identifiers describe the molecule, not a vial. Confirming a specific lot takes analytical data: a mass result consistent with the reference mass and a chromatographic purity result, both tied to that lot number.

problemSolution.problem: What does the Semax sequence actually tell me?
problemSolution.solution: MEHFPGP is seven residues: methionine, glutamic acid, histidine, phenylalanine, proline, glycine and proline. The first four (MEHF) match the ACTH(4-7) region. The last three (PGP) are an added Pro-Gly-Pro extension, which is thought to slow peptidase attack (Potaman et al., 1991).
problemSolution.explanation: The sequence matters when you compare supplier documents. Names and abbreviations vary, but a genuine Semax record should resolve to these same seven residues in this order. A different length, order or terminal modification describes a different compound.

problemSolution.problem: Is Semax the same molecule as ACTH?
problemSolution.solution: No. ACTH is a 39-amino-acid hormone. Semax is a seven-residue synthetic peptide related to a short region of it. FDA's review, citing earlier literature, describes the ACTH(4-10) fragment as lacking the hormonal (corticotropic and melanotropic) properties of full-length ACTH.
problemSolution.explanation: In practice, findings about ACTH the hormone do not transfer to Semax, and Semax findings do not describe ACTH. Treat them as separate molecules that share ancestry.

problemSolution.problem: How should I distinguish Semax from ACTH(4-10), ACTH(4-7), and Pro-Gly-Pro?
problemSolution.solution: The four names describe four different sequences: Semax is MEHFPGP, ACTH(4-7) is MEHF, ACTH(4-10) is MEHFRWG, and Pro-Gly-Pro is PGP. Semax is a synthetic analogue related to the ACTH(4-10) region, with a different sequence: it keeps MEHF and replaces the last three residues with PGP. Calculated average masses run about 814, 563, 962 and 269 g/mol respectively.
problemSolution.explanation: Similar names cause real errors. A literature search on "ACTH(4-10) analog" can pull in unrelated results, and a procurement record that says only "ACTH fragment" is ambiguous. N-acetyl Semax and Adamax refer to related but distinct compounds and should not be treated as interchangeable with Semax.

problemSolution.problem: What does the Semax–BDNF research actually show?
problemSolution.solution: A rat hippocampal study (Dolotov et al., 2006) reported increased BDNF protein, TrkB phosphorylation and BDNF mRNA following Semax exposure; the largest BDNF protein rise was about 1.4-fold. A companion basal-forebrain paper reported specific binding and higher BDNF protein, and earlier glial-culture work reported NGF and BDNF mRNA induction (Shadrina et al., 2001).
problemSolution.explanation: Taken together, these studies link Semax to changes in neurotrophin markers in those systems. They do not identify the receptor, and FDA's 2026 review states that the mechanism of Semax gene regulation is unknown. They also come from rat and cell models, so they do not translate automatically to humans.

problemSolution.problem: What does “neuroprotective” mean in Semax research?
problemSolution.solution: In experimental work, neuroprotection means a measured difference in an injury model compared with a control group. It might be a change in gene or protein markers, or a smaller damaged area. It is a description of a result, not a promise.
problemSolution.explanation: In rat cerebral-ischemia models, Semax altered neurotrophin transcripts (Dmitrieva et al., 2010) and immune-response and vascular genes (Medvedeva et al., 2014). Later work reported lower inflammatory-gene expression and changes in MMP-9, c-Fos, JNK and CREB (Filippenkov et al., 2020; Sudarkina et al., 2021). These are molecular readouts in animals. They do not show that Semax protects the human brain.

problemSolution.problem: What do Semax cognitive and behavioral findings actually tell a researcher?
problemSolution.solution: The animal findings are specific. The 2006 hippocampal study reported more conditioned avoidance reactions in Semax-treated rats alongside its BDNF results. In a rat photothrombotic-ischemia study, Semax-treated animals did not show the memory-retention deficit seen in vehicle-treated animals (Romanova et al., 2006, as summarized in FDA's briefing).
problemSolution.explanation: Human reports come from historical clinical literature, mostly stroke-related and mostly Russian. That literature is limited, as the research-limits section below explains. Together, these findings tell a researcher which endpoints have been examined. They do not support a cognitive-enhancement claim, and this page does not make one.

problemSolution.problem: What should I understand when searching for “Semax benefits”?
problemSolution.solution: In research writing, a benefit is not a product promise. It usually means a reported biological, molecular or behavioral finding in one study. Examples include higher BDNF protein in rat hippocampus, or a smaller infarcted area in a rat ischemia model (about 20% smaller in the Romanova study).
problemSolution.explanation: Consumer pages often blend such findings with claims that no study tested. So when you meet the word, ask four questions: which species or system, which comparator, which endpoint, and which chemical form. This page reports findings. It does not say what Semax will do for anyone.

problemSolution.problem: How should I interpret “Semax dosage” searches?
problemSolution.solution: Published doses and historical pharmaceutical administration parameters belong to their own research contexts. Each depends on the species, the preparation, the chemical form and the purpose of the study, and none transfers to another setting. FDA's review also notes that many clinical reports do not say which form of Semax was used.
problemSolution.explanation: Veracue does not provide human-use dosing or administration guidance, and this page lists no doses, schedules or routes. That applies to every dosage-related query, including searches for spray and injectable formats. Researchers set experimental concentrations through their own validated study design and the primary literature.

problemSolution.problem: How is Semax different from Selank?
problemSolution.solution: They are different molecules with a shared ending. Semax (MEHFPGP) derives from an ACTH fragment. Selank (Thr-Lys-Pro-Arg-Pro-Gly-Pro) is described as a tuftsin analogue. Both have seven residues and both end in Pro-Gly-Pro, but their first four residues differ, and so do their average masses (about 813.9 and 751.9 g/mol).
problemSolution.explanation: Both have experimental literature and some historical clinical literature. The table below sets them side by side without ranking them. For Veracue's Selank information, see the Selank page.

problemSolution.problem: What should I look for on a Semax COA?
problemSolution.solution: A certificate of analysis documents one lot, so read it as a set of linked facts. A Semax COA may include the lot number, product identity, purity, the HPLC or UPLC method, a mass spectrometry result, the molecular form, the testing laboratory and the test date. It may also report peptide or water content. The checklist below lists each field.
problemSolution.explanation: Check that the pieces agree. In FDA's review, certificates titled Semax Acetate carried the free peptide's CAS number, formula and molecular weight, which left the described substance unclear. A COA is only as useful as its consistency with the vial in hand.

problemSolution.problem: What can the Veracue Semax page establish — and what requires lot-specific documentation?
problemSolution.solution: This page can establish molecular reference information: the sequence, formula and weight, the relationship to ACTH fragments, the published research context and how Semax compares with Selank. It cannot establish what is in a particular vial.
problemSolution.explanation: Lot-specific documentation is required for the actual purity, the actual analytical results, the lot identity, the salt or counterion, and any product-specific testing. Chemistry describes the target, and testing describes the sample. Keeping those apart is what makes the reference material on this page trustworthy.

massSpectrometry.title: Chromatography and Mass Spectrometry: Two Different Questions
body: Chromatography and mass spectrometry answer different questions. HPLC helps assess chromatographic purity. Mass spectrometry helps assess molecular identity and mass. Neither one alone establishes every aspect of material quality, and a single mass peak does not prove identity by itself.
HPLC purity should be interpreted together with the chromatographic method and detection conditions reported on the applicable analytical record.

For Semax, the calculated monoisotopic mass is approximately 813.348 Da. The observed m/z depends on the charge state and on ion or adduct conditions, so a report should not be judged against one universal value. Methionine oxidation can produce a mass shift of approximately +16 Da, so oxidation-related species may appear in an MS dataset. Interpretation should be based on the complete analytical spectrum and method.

researchLimitations.title: What the Evidence Can and Cannot Tell You
researchLimitations.intro: Historical clinical literature on Semax exists, and it stays on this page. It is not evidence for the Veracue research material.
points: Gusev et al. (1997) compared 30 acute-stroke patients receiving Semax within combined therapy with 80 patients on conventional therapy, and reported some influence on recovery rate. Gusev et al. (2018) followed 110 post-stroke patients with and without Semax and reported higher plasma BDNF and faster Barthel-index improvement in the Semax subgroups.
These were comparative studies of modest size. Their abstracts do not describe placebo control.

Comparator groups differ between papers, and most of the literature comes from one geographic and linguistic setting. FDA's 2026 briefing did not evaluate Russian-language studies, and it found no human pharmacokinetic studies.
The clinical papers rarely say whether they used the free peptide or a salt, so they cannot be matched to a specific research lot.
A historical pharmaceutical preparation and a current research lot are different things. Findings from one do not carry over to the other.
FDA's 2026 briefing describes Semax as a registered drug in Russia. Semax is not an FDA-approved drug in the United States. Regulatory materials change, so check current FDA sources.
